moments.title: Stocks are just one room in a much bigger house
moments.summary: The opening line of the lesson: most people equate investing with stocks, and the speaker reframes stocks as one room in a much bigger house.
moments.evidence: When most people hear the word investing, they think of one thing, stocks. But stocks are just one room in a much bigger house.

moments.title: An asset is simply where your money lives
moments.summary: The definition given in the lesson: when you invest, your money has to live somewhere, and that somewhere is an asset — a savings account, a bond, gold, a stock or real estate.
moments.evidence: When you invest, your money has to live somewhere. That somewhere is an asset.

moments.title: Every asset has a different personality
moments.summary: The lesson closes on the idea that assets behave differently — some favour stability, some chase growth, some are highly unpredictable, and some become popular in uncertain times.
moments.evidence: every asset has a different personality. Some love stability, some chase growth and some are highly unpredictable.
